newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to talk to debtors if no Paris Club deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia to talk to debtors if no Paris Club deal.

text.p: Russia will resume debt talks with countries also owing money to governments grouped in the Paris Club if it fails to reach agreement on joining the Club before the G-7 meeting in Denver, a senior Finance Ministry official said.
Russia has applied to join the Paris Club and the decision is to be announced by the Denver meeting June 20-22.

While in talks with the Paris Club, Russia suspended talks with debtor countries which have signed restructuring agreements with the Club. These countries are not paying their debt to Russia while they wait to see whether it will join the Club.

"If we fail to make progress on major issues with the Paris Club by that time, Russia is unlikely to keep up a moratorium any longer on regulating the debt of countries which applied to the Paris Club for restructuring," Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters in a weekend interview.
"We can wait no longer, it costs too much."
Countries already in debt agreements with the Paris Club owe Russia $37 billion. Altogether Russia is owed $132 billion in debts inherited from the former Soviet Union.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said last week Russia would press ahead to get repaid by Libya and Iraq, which owe $2.5 billion and $7 billion respectively.
Russia itself has reached agreement on rescheduling $40 billion it owed members of the Paris Club, and this agreement opens the way to Russia joining as a creditor.
